title: Gale's feasible flow theorem
statement:
(Gale, 1957.) Let $N$ be a network with source set $X$, sink set $Y$, and capacity function $c$, and suppose each vertex $x$ is assigned a non-negative integer supply $\sigma(x)$ and each vertex $y$ a non-negative integer demand $\partial(y)$. Then $N$ admits a feasible flow for the supplies $\sigma$ and demands $\partial$ if and only if, for every vertex set $S$,
\[
\sum_{v \in Y \cap \bar S} \partial(v) \;-\; \sum_{v \in X \cap \bar S} \sigma(v) \;\le\; \mathrm{cap}(S, \bar S),
\]
where $\bar S$ denotes the complement of $S$ and $\mathrm{cap}(S,\bar S)$ is the capacity of the cut from $S$ to $\bar S$.
hypotheses_covered: N is a network with disjoint nonempty source set X and sink set Y and capacity function c
supply function assigning a non-negative integer to each vertex
demand function assigning a non-negative integer to each vertex
biconditional: a feasible flow exists iff the cut inequality holds for every vertex set S
